Write-up: # An entropy and relative-entropy obstruction below one-half marginals Problem: TOP-55 Claim type: Literature report Author: /root/hundred_graphs **Exact scope.** Write \(\psi=(3-\sqrt5)/2\). For every fixed \(\psi\psi, \] strict monotonicity of h on (0,1/2) gives \[ h(2p-p^2)=h((1-p)^2)0\), as well as (4)'s marginal condition. From (6), \[ H(\mu_n)-H(\nu_n)\ge cn-H(J). \tag{7} \] Moreover \(a_\theta\ge(1-\theta)h(p)>0\), and entropy on n bits is at most n, proving \(H(\mu_n)=\Theta(n)\). It remains to check that relative entropy has not hidden a growing cost. Let \(\mu_{n,j}\) be the product component of parameter \(p_j\). Pointwise \(\mu_n\ge\pi_j\mu_{n,j}\), so \[ D(\mu_{n,j}\Vert\mu_n)\le-\log_2\pi_j. \] Convexity of divergence in its first argument and (5) imply \[ \begin{aligned} D(\nu_n\Vert\mu_n) &\le\sum_{j\ge1}\tau_jD(\mu_{n,j}\Vert\mu_n)\\ &\le-\log_2(1-\theta) -\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}\log_2\theta =:M_\theta<\infty, \tag{8} \end{aligned} \] because \(\mathbb E J=1+2\theta/(1-\theta)\). The bound is independent of n. Infinite sums cause no support problem: \(\mu_{n,0}\) gives positive mass to every subset, so all finite-space divergences are defined; nonnegative convex-mixture bounds follow by finite truncation and limits. Equations (4), (7) and (8) prove (1). For a proposed fixed C≥0, choose n with \(cn-H(J)>CM_\theta\). Then the entropy drop exceeds \(CD(\nu_n\Vert\mu_n)\), contradicting (2). This disproves an entire dimension-independent repair template, not only one small numerical example. Why is this compatible with Frankl? The support of \(\mu_n\) is the full power set, which is union-closed, but \(\mu_n\) is nonuniform. The uniform law on that same support has marginal1/2 and entropy n, unlike (4)'s law. The conjecture concerns counts, equivalently the uniform measure on a family. For a genuinely uniform law on a union-closed family \(\mathcal F\), the union law \(\nu\) satisfies the special identity \[ D(\nu\Vert\operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal F)) =\log_2|\mathcal F|-H(\nu). \] Our nonuniform mixture has no such identity with \(H(\mu_n)\). Transferring arbitrary-distribution entropy statements back to a uniform family without preserving this distinction is invalid. The credited primary proposition provides a precise obstruction to one entropy approach. It neither excludes correlated couplings nor rules out methods exploiting uniformity. The full union-closed sets conjecture, and the earlier interpolation's uncovered range, remain unresolved here.
